Subject: Official response: tenant clinic this Saturday

We’ve seen the concerns raised here, and we understand why people are upset. Getting a lawyer’s letter shortly after asking for help can be frightening. We’re sorry people are facing that worry, and we want to share what we can without discussing anyone’s individual situation.

Cascade Legal Rights Project does not share, sell, or disclose clinic attendees’ information to landlords or their attorneys. Sign-in records are kept internally in locked storage.

Eviction filings in Magistrate Court are public records, and some law firms use those records to send mailings to tenants. Public filings are a likely explanation for why someone might receive a letter; we can’t determine the source of any individual mailing here.

The free tenant rights clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. The library room is closed, so we’ve moved the clinic to Mt. Zion Fellowship Hall in East Atlanta. The accessible side entrance is by the parking lot. People are still welcome, and no appointment is needed.

If you have questions, email clinic@cascaderights.example or call our office at 404-555-0187. We won’t discuss anyone’s attendance or circumstances in this thread. We hope this information is helpful to neighbors deciding whether to come.
